title: The same operation
promptMarkdown:
In under 200 words and without the text open, explain two things.

1. Why $GL_2(\mathbb R)$ is a group, yet is **not** a subgroup of $(M_2(\mathbb R),+)$, the additive group of all $2\times2$ real matrices, even though it is a subset of it. Say precisely what the definition of subgroup requires beyond "a subset that happens to be a group".
2. Why $(\mathbb Z_n,\cdot)$ is not a group while $U(n)$ is, naming the axiom that fails for $\mathbb Z_n$ and the one non-obvious condition that must be checked for $U(n)$.
hintLadder: Which operation does the subgroup definition refer to: the subset's own, or the ambient group's? Test closure of $GL_2(\mathbb R)$ under the ambient operation.
In $U(n)$, is the product of two units a unit? That is the condition to check; the others are inherited.

criteria.criterion: States that a subgroup must be a group under the ambient group's operation, and shows GL_2(R) fails closure under addition (e.g. A + (−A) = 0 is singular), while being a group under multiplication.

levels.label: met

levels.label: partially met
levels.description: Requirement stated without an explicit failure, or vice versa.

criteria.criterion: Names inverses as the failing axiom for (Z_n, ·) (0, and any a with gcd(a, n) > 1) and identifies closure of U(n) under multiplication as the condition that needs proof.
Within the word limit and free of unsupported claims.
